Name: Stardew i18n Translator
Author: Neko41
Description:
[b]Stardew i18n Translator 2.0.0[/b]

A portable Windows x64 desktop app for translating Stardew Valley and SMAPI mod localization files without editing large JSON files by hand.

[b]Translation workflow[/b]

[list]
[*][b]Scan[/b] a Stardew Valley Mods folder for standard
[b]i18n/default.json[/b]
source files and existing target-language translations. Scanning is read-only.[/*]
[*][b]Work from Overview and Workspace[/b] with progress summaries, search, status and validation filters, resizable panels and columns, keyboard shortcuts, multi-select, and batch actions.[/*]
[*][b]Handle multi-component mods[/b] as one package while preserving every component folder during import and translation ZIP export.[/*]
[*][b]Track English source changes[/b] between complete scans, including added, changed, and removed strings.[/*]
[*][b]Review safely[/b] with protected-token checks for Stardew, SMAPI, Content Patcher, dialogue, mail, placeholders, and formatting values.[/*]
[*][b]Undo recent edits[/b] and reopen dismissible operation results with paths, filenames, and copyable details.[/*]
[*][b]Import and export[/b] existing translations, direct target-language JSON files, external LLM batches, and installable translation ZIPs.[/*]
[/list]
The app uses four clear translation states: [b]Open[/b], [b]Changed[/b], [b]Review[/b], and [b]Done[/b]. Blocking validation findings are displayed separately from translation status.

[b]Every AI-generated or externally imported suggestion enters Review. AI output is never marked Done automatically.[/b]

[b]Optional AI assistance[/b]

AI is optional. Manual translation, scanning, validation, glossary building, import, and export work without it.

[list]
[*][b]Local AI[/b] connects only to a localhost service you configure, such as Ollama or LM Studio.[/*]
[*][b]Codex CLI[/b] uses a separately installed Codex CLI and its existing ChatGPT sign-in and account limits. The app does not read, copy, or store CLI credentials. Model selection and usage information are shown only when the installed CLI reports them.[/*]
[*][b]External LLM batch[/b] exports a self-contained JSON file for a file-capable LLM and validates the returned file before importing anything.[/*]
[/list]
Large Codex selections are split into bounded, context-aware batches with visible progress and cancellation. A quality review and focused repair stages check meaning, natural phrasing, terminology, grammar, register, speaker voice, dialogue continuity, and protected tokens.

These additional Codex review and repair calls are enabled by default and can be disabled to reduce processing time and token use. The app shows a warning because first drafts may then need more manual correction.

When an AI run starts, the selected English source, limited neighboring English context, and matching glossary terms are sent only to the chosen backend.

[b]Optional glossary[/b]

Build a high-confidence, language-specific glossary from local Stardew string data or a compatible installed community language pack. Glossary terms can help keep item, NPC, location, tool, weapon, clothing, and season names consistent. The glossary is built locally and is never required for normal translation or export.

[b]Safety and local data[/b]

[list]
[*]Scanning does not modify installed mods.[/*]
[*]Settings, glossary caches, and translation work are stored beside the executable in the portable
[b]data/[/b]
folder.[/*]
[*]Installed target-language files are changed only when you explicitly export.[/*]
[*]Direct export validates the complete scope, creates visible backups for existing target files, and rolls back earlier files if a later multi-file write fails.[/*]
[*]External batch imports reject stale or mismatched results and preserve existing non-empty local translations.[/*]
[/list][b]Supported target languages[/b]

[b]Built into Stardew Valley:[/b]
German (de), Spanish (es), French (fr), Hungarian (hu), Italian (it), Japanese (ja), Korean (ko), Portuguese (pt), Russian (ru), Turkish (tr), and Chinese (zh).

[b]Curated custom-language targets:[/b]
Vietnamese (vi), Indonesian (id), Ukrainian (uk), Polish (pl), Finnish (fi), Dutch (nl), Czech (cs), and Thai (th).

Custom-language files can be translated and exported normally, but using them in Stardew requires a matching custom-language mod.

[b]Installation & updates[/b]

[list=1]
[*]Download the portable ZIP from the Files tab.[/*]
[*]Extract the complete folder to a writable location. There is no installer.[/*]
[*]Run [b]stardew-i18n-translator.exe[/b].[/*]
[*]Choose the Stardew Valley folder, Mods folder, and target language.[/*]
[/list]
For an update, close the app and replace the executable and README with the files from the new ZIP. Keep the existing [b]data/[/b] folder beside the executable so settings, glossary caches, and translation work remain available.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the executable is unsigned. Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime is required and is already included with Windows 11 and most Windows 10 systems.

[b]Scope & source[/b]

This tool targets standard SMAPI localization files: [b]<mod>/i18n/default.json[/b] and [b]<mod>/i18n/<language>.json[/b]. It is not a mod manager or a general Stardew JSON/XNB editor, and it does not translate arbitrary Content Patcher data files.
